title: Raspberry Jam-Filled Berliner Doughnuts
summary: Pillowy round yeast doughnuts fried golden with a pale middle band and piped full of seedless raspberry jam.
equipment: stand mixer with dough hook (or large bowl)
2 baking trays lined with oiled baking paper
large heavy pan or casserole, at least 24 cm wide
wire rack over a tray lined with kitchen paper
piping bag with a long narrow nozzle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Make a silky dough
steps.text: Stir the flour, sugar, yeast and salt together, pour in the warm milk and egg and knead for 5 min. Work in the softened butter bit by bit, then knead 6-8 min longer until the dough looks silky and comes away cleanly from the bowl. A well-developed dough traps the gas that makes these so light.

steps.title: First rise
steps.text: Cover and set aside in a warm spot for 1-1.5 h until doubled.

steps.title: Stamp out rounds
steps.text: Knock the dough back, roll it 1.5 cm thick and cut 8 cm rounds without a hole. Press the trimmings together and roll once more so you have 12. Space them well apart on the oiled paper, since they spread as they prove.

steps.title: Second rise
steps.text: Lay a sheet of cling film loosely over the top and prove for 40-50 min. They are ready once they look risen, soft and pillowy.

steps.title: Bring the oil to temperature
steps.text: Fill the heavy pan with about 4 cm of oil, no more than half its depth, and heat to 170 °C. A slightly lower heat than for rings gives the thicker rounds time to cook through before they brown too much.

steps.title: Fry until golden
steps.text: Cook 3 at a time for about 2 min per side, keeping the oil between 165 and 175 °C. Each should be evenly golden with a pale band round its waist and read about 90 °C in the middle. Drain on the rack, then let them cool for 15 min so the crumb sets before filling.

steps.title: Pipe in the jam
steps.text: Push a chopstick into the side of each doughnut to the centre and twist gently to open a pocket. Pipe in about 25 g jam per doughnut, stopping when it feels heavier and a little jam peeps out of the hole.

tips: A common mistake is filling them hot; warm doughnuts tear and the jam leaks, so wait the full 15 min.
Seedless jam pipes smoothly through a narrow nozzle; sieve jam with seeds first.
If they brown before the centre reaches about 90 °C, lower the oil temperature slightly for the next batch.
Roll them in caster sugar while warm if you prefer a sugared finish.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Eat on the day of frying for the best texture. Leftovers keep loosely covered at room temperature for up to 1 day.
